summary: An ISSTA 2026 empirical study of model editing (UltraEdit, DINM, token-wise DEFER*) as a way to harden open-weight code LLMs against generating vulnerable code, compared with the inference-time method CoSec on six 3B-8B models. Editing raises CodeQL-measured security on the 9 trained CWEs but transfers unreliably to 17 unseen CWEs and hurts HumanEval correctness; the authors then propose SafeEdit (functional tuning on Code Evol-Instruct with a regulariser anchoring UltraEdit-modified parameters) and evaluate it on eight models.

claims.claim: Model editing improves security ratio by 15-25% over vanilla on seen CWEs, more than CoSec, and is stable under prompt perturbations.
claims.evidence: §3.1 RQ1.1 tables and Finding text (line ~126); perturbation set built from a single scenario (CWE-089 0-Py) for RQ1.2. 25 completions x 10 seeds x 3 temperatures.

claims.claim: Editing gains transfer unreliably to unseen CWEs and can reduce functional correctness.
claims.evidence: §3.2 (29 scenarios over 17 unseen CWEs, disjoint CodeQL rules) and §3.3 Table 4 HumanEval Pass@k; CoSec stays near vanilla on unseen CWEs.

claims.claim: SafeEdit improves Pass@1 over UltraEdit by +11.73/+13.70/+15.50 points at T=0.1/0.4/0.8 while largely preserving security, and beats CoSec on security by +7.54% to +12.04% relative.
claims.evidence: §3.4.1, Table 6; Table 7 Wilcoxon over 8 LLMs (SR vs CoSec p≤0.039, Cliff's δ 0.438-0.688). Security vs UltraEdit changes +7.44/-0.28/-3.48 points, so 'largely preserving' holds. Pass@1 recovery comes from instruction tuning on Code Evol-Instruct, with no reported decontamination against HumanEval.

claims.claim: SafeEdit improves joint secure-and-correct generation on CodeGuard+.
claims.evidence: Table 8: SP@1 improves over vanilla on all eight models (5.41% to 20.29% relative); CodeGuard+ uses CodeQL+SonarQube ensemble and unit tests, 91 prompts, 34 CWEs in Python and C/C++.

patterns.note: Parameter-level hardening works on trained CWEs but generalises poorly and costs correctness unless followed by regularised tuning.

CodeQL used as the security oracle (37/40 agreement with manual inspection); authors stress it is an evaluation proxy, not a defense. Implicitly supports keeping static analysis as the gate since model-level fixes miss unseen CWEs.

methodology.sample: 710 vulnerable/fixed pairs (9 CWEs, Python and C/C++) for editing; D_sec 9 CWEs x 3 prompts; 29 unseen-CWE scenarios over 17 CWEs; HumanEval 164; MultiPL-E (C++/JS/TS); CodeGuard+ 91 prompts.
methodology.baselines: Vanilla, CoSec (current inference-time SOTA, official implementation), UltraEdit, DINM, DEFER*; fine-tuning comparison in §4.4.
methodology.models: LLaMA-3.1-8B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B, CodeGen-6B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B/3B; plus StarCoder-3B/7B for SafeEdit. All small open-weight, several dated.
methodology.variance: 10 random seeds, 25 completions per prompt, three temperatures; Wilcoxon signed-rank and Cliff's delta across models.
methodology.ablations: Suffix length L, efficiency, SafeEdit vs fine-tuning, combination with CoSec, unseen-CWE generalisation.
methodology.contamination_controls: Seen/unseen CWE sets disjoint (Jaccard 0); Evol-Instruct tuning data stated to not overlap the editing set, but no HumanEval decontamination reported.
methodology.languages: Python and C/C++ for security; HumanEval Python; MultiPL-E C++/JavaScript/TypeScript. No Java.

standards.artifacts: Code at github.com/swf1996120/SafeEdit; replication package referenced for perturbations and full results.

biases.detail: SafeEdit is the authors' method, evaluated on their chosen pipeline, though with external CodeGuard+ check.
Functional recovery tuning on Code Evol-Instruct then measured on HumanEval with no decontamination stated.
Security ratio is a CodeQL proxy over short completions (256 tokens) of templated prompts, not real-world secure-by-construction code.
Function-level completions from small prompt suites (27 seen-CWE prompts), not repository-level or agentic generation.
Model editing needs parameter access; inapplicable to API models used by commercial agent hosts (acknowledged).

verdict_reason: Peer-reviewed, multi-model, seeded and statistically tested with released code; but function-level, small open models only, CodeQL-proxy security, no Java, and the technique cannot be applied to the hosted models an agent harness uses.
applicability: Low direct transfer. The Java team consumes hosted models through mixed agent hosts and cannot edit weights, so SafeEdit itself is unusable. The transferable finding is negative for model-side hardening: security gains do not generalise to unseen CWE types and trade off correctness. That argues for keeping deterministic static analysis (CodeQL/Semgrep/local Sonar with Java rules) as a gate in the agent loop across all ingestion repos instead of trusting any 'secure-tuned' model, and for encoding security requirements (input validation, injection-safe persistence for ingested content) as explicit acceptance criteria in specs.
